title: Desk Terms for Agreeing a Change to an Approved Specification
content:
# Desk Terms for Agreeing a Change to an Approved Specification

## Terms in force

A change to the specification of a commission under Belrose Design Studio Custom Commissions is agreed only when the request reaches the studio within the change order window in calendar days, counted from the date the customer approved the design. The change order window is counted in whole calendar days from the day the design was approved, that day counting as day zero, weekends and studio holidays included. No more changes are agreed on one commission than the programme allows, and a request beyond that count is refused rather than absorbed. A change agreed while the piece is in production puts the commission on hold until the revised specification is written, and the promised delivery date is moved out accordingly. The change itself is agreed by the customer on the commission service request record, because committing to a different piece at a different price is theirs alone to do.

## The window, element by element

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| The clock starts | The date the customer approved the design, as recorded on the commission |
| Counting | Whole calendar days, the approval day counting as day zero, weekends and studio holidays included |
| Length | The programme's change order window in calendar days |
| Direction | The request must reach the studio not later than the last day of the window |
| The boundary day | A request reaching the studio on the last day of the window is within it |
| Evidence | The commission record, correlated by its commission reference; the customer's recollection of the approval date does not stand in for it |

A request that reaches the studio after the window has run is not agreed.

## The count of changes

The changes already priced onto the commission are counted over the whole life of the commission, from the consultation to the day the request is handled. Where that count has reached the programme's ceiling on changes agreed on one commission, the request is refused rather than absorbed.

## Both sides of the window (hypothetical)

Under a programme whose window is 10 calendar days, with the design approved on the 1st of a month: a request reaching the studio on the 11th, which is day 10, is within the window; a request reaching the studio on the 12th, which is day 11, is not.

## Term no longer in force

One sentence of the earlier wording of these terms has been superseded by the current basis and is **no longer in force**:

> "A change to the specification after the design has been approved is agreed as a change order, priced on its own and charged with the programme's change administration fee." — no longer in force.
